beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. The entry point takes --url out first, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Two commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder, whose headless browser opens the server's own page: the page plays the walkthrough, the Codex voice narrates it, and the tab's capture becomes the video file.

nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.name: Command contract
nodes.responsibility: Runs one bound command contract: parse, prerequisites, handler, presentation; callers reach it only through its root files
nodes.description: Callers outside import only the root files of src/cli/command-contract. runner.ts exports runCommand, the one call the router makes; it passes straight on to executeCommand in lib/execution.ts, which is private. bootstrap.ts and status.ts are root files too: the bootstrap bin.ts runs first, and the status command contract.

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.description: Callers outside import only the root files of src/cli/command-contract. runner.ts exports runCommand, the one call the router makes; it passes straight on to executeCommand in lib/execution.ts, which is private. bootstrap.ts and status.ts are root files too: the bootstrap bin.ts runs first, and the status command contract.

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. The entry point takes --url out first, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.
